title: Federated Learning System for Hospital Imaging Models
technical_field: Medical imaging and distributed machine learning
problem: Hospitals cannot pool patient scans to train diagnostic image models because of privacy rules, and models trained on one site generalize poorly to scanners and populations at other sites.
solution: Each hospital trains a local neural network on its own scans and sends only encrypted weight updates to a coordinating server. The server weights each update by a site data-quality score, aggregates them into a global model, and returns the model for the next round. A differential privacy noise stage is applied to updates before they leave the hospital.

elements.text: A local training module at each hospital that trains a neural network on locally stored medical images without exporting the images
Encryption of model weight updates before transmission to a coordinating server
A server-side aggregation module that combines the weight updates into a global model
A per-site data-quality score computed from label consistency and image acquisition metadata
Weighting of each site update during aggregation by its data-quality score
A differential privacy noise stage applied to the weight updates before they leave the hospital
Redistribution of the global model to the hospitals for a further training round

dependent_features: The quality score is recomputed each round
Convergence is detected when the global validation loss changes by less than a threshold
